screen.title: Ted Lasso
screen.plot: In a shock development struggling English Premier League team AFC Richmond hires American football coach Ted Lasso as its new manager. Lasso knows nothing about soccer/football. With unshakable enthusiasm and positivity he rises to the challenge but little known to him there are forces within the club that don't want him to succeed.
screen.awards: Won 13 Primetime Emmys. 75 wins & 213 nominations total
notes: Definitely a feel-good show. I like it a lot. Honestly, it makes me want to coach again. I kinda miss coaching baseball and having an impact on the kids.

Ted Lasso is just such a likable guy. I don’t necessarily like how the show portrays everything as somehow going right or being part of some deeper plan of his, but I guess you can get away with that in fiction. What I really admire is the way he conducts and carries himself. He makes you believe in him because he genuinely believes in himself and the people around him. That kind of confidence and optimism is infectious.

Hard to believe it came out in 2020—that was six years ago. And here I am, just now getting on the bandwagon. On a side note, I’m glad I’m finally putting my Apple TV subscription through my Chase Sapphire Reserve to good use. Gotta make the most of those card benefits.

Anyways, I digress. I really just wanted to say how much I like this show. There’s something genuinely refreshing about its optimism, especially when it comes to believing in people and bringing out the best in them. It reminds me of what I loved about coaching in the first place.
I think I really needed a show like this at this point in my life.

presently.label: Working on
presently.text: I love that it is now Fall. I feel motivated. I like the cold weather a lot. I'm still working on school research stuff. I'm trying on reducing mental stress so as to provide more bandwidth for retaining information. I've mentioned in a previous post about how difficult it is to learn now, but ai honestly think being stressed just filters any retentive learning.

presently.label: Reading
presently.text: I haven't read many new books. I've actually been watching more things because there is less exertion of cognitive efford required. I did see that [Reader](https://readwise.io/accounts/login/?next=/to_reader) is introducing some sort of eBook store which would be neat to see their expansion.

presently.label: Small pleasure
presently.text: I moved my desk to be next to my bed. Now it's easier to begin working on stuff at my desk. I also got a cabinet for my room to store my kitchen tchotchkes. A less cluttered room is a small pleasure.

presently.label: Recent discovery
presently.text: I've recently rediscovered the motivation to just do things. I've been so previously burnt out that I literally could not muster the compelling motivation or spirit to do something as simple as hang up a cardigan fron the day. I literally was in mental anguish and could not compel myself to just do simple tasks, so my room would accumulate with disorganized clutter. It was very very extremely uncharacteristic of me. I don't exactly know the cause—perhaps fully saturated cognitive inputs or being burnt out or whatever. But in any case, I recently rediscovered my innate lifelong ability to just do things without any mental drag. Perhaps the changing of seasons and cooler temperature has helped return me?

presently.label: Looking forward to
presently.text: Looking forward to the weather getting even cooler. I like the way the air smells in the fall/winter. i might put on constant gilmore girls in the background or sappy hallmark movies. i started with christmas land from 2015 today. I look forward to writing these monthly /now updates because it allows me to be reflective momentarily (as if I'm not already...?) I am reflective, iI guess I meant that I like this processing forcing myself to write, but i already journal, so its not that either. I guess frankly i do this on the offchance that someone wants a contemporary view into my thoughts? but there really isnt much careful gleaning to gather here since there isn't elaborate thought guaranteed here. idk im rambling at this point but i guess this is just cooler to have than traditional social media... its a fun coding endeavor too i guess, getting this to this point?

presently.label: One open question
presently.text: I'm not quite sure. I had to pause for a minute to seriously scrounge up some new philosophical questions I've had. I think as of recent, I've been just trying to "be" more than be introspective. I think maybe this is just more of an open question for myself—how to really make valuable use of my time? I'm actually okay with just sitting and being in silence and not have competing worry about spending my time otherwise. I think this may be a period of just offloading congnitive build up — plaque— eroding my ability to be presently immersed in the moment.

presently.label: Something I recommend
presently.text: Obsidian—I've been using it for years. Especially now with the importance of knowing how to code. I think Obsidian is part of integral digital literacy. I should probably make a video sometime documenting it all, but what I've learned from writing my book is that many people would not use it. I'm sure a select few of precociously motivated individuals would seek it out, but its that people just don't know obsidian or know why they would need it... whatever, it doesn't matter, it's okay. I could teach whoever if they are curious. I guess my recommendation is just keeping to yourself and leaving things unsaid unless they are better said. Being able to read the room is my recommendation. As compassionate as you may think by offering your service, people frankly just don't care as much as you do, so let it go.
